extra.message: Session tokens are HMAC'd with a hardcoded APP_SECRET ('foo123bar', defined in secrets/index.js). Session.verify() only checks hash(username|id) against this static, source-controlled secret. Because /user/all (user.js) leaks every user's username_hash, password_hash, and session_id with no authentication, and the secret itself is public in source, an attacker who knows a target's plaintext username can compute hash(username) to match it against the leaked username_hash, recover that user's session_id from the same leaked row, and then construct a forged session_str = `username|session_id|hash(username|session_id)` that passes Session.verify() and the /user/authenticated session_id check — a full authentication bypass without ever knowing the password.

GET /user/all runs 'SELECT * FROM users' and returns every row as JSON with no authentication or authorization check. This exposes username_hash, password_hash, and session_id for every user in the system to any unauthenticated caller.

extra.message: GET /user/logout performs a state-changing action (clears session_id in DB, clears session cookie) and relies solely on the session cookie for authentication. The cookie set in set_session_cookie (lines 15-21) has no SameSite attribute and there is no CSRF token, so a cross-site request (e.g. an tag on an attacker page) will carry the session cookie automatically and force a logout.
